title: Synoptic wind-driven control of hypoxia off the Pearl River Estuary
query: Using the supplied CMOMS daily oxygen, temperature, salinity, chlorophyll and velocity for May-September 2011-2020, test the following findings of Li et al. (2021, Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans, doi:10.1029/2020JC016700) on summer hypoxia off the Pearl River Estuary: (1) bottom hypoxia in the coastal transition zones west and east of the estuary varies strongly in space and time with synoptic changes of the summer monsoon; (2) under upwelling-favourable winds the northeastward shelf current converges with the river plume, strengthening stratification and favouring hypoxia; (3) when upwelling-favourable winds relax or turn downwelling-favourable, the plume and organic matter are carried westward, vertical mixing weakens, hypoxia is enhanced in the western zone and the opposite happens in the eastern zone; (4) once the downwelling-favourable wind relaxes, conditions return to their upwelling-period state. Winds are not supplied: identify the wind regimes from the ocean data and explain how. Define the zones and the hypoxia threshold you use, give a verdict for each finding (reproduced, partly reproduced, not reproduced, or not testable with the supplied data) with quantitative evidence, and explain differences from the paper.

paper.title: Spatiotemporal Development and Dissipation of Hypoxia Induced by Variable Wind‐Driven Shelf Circulation off the Pearl River Estuary: Observational and Modeling Studies
